description: A one-voice drum sequencer: eight patterns of sixteen steps, each step with its own velocity, accent and chance of firing, edited on the display and clocked from outside

inputs.text: Each rise advances the pattern by one step, wrapping at the pattern's own length
Each rise counts one bar and, once the current pattern has had its repeats, moves to the next active pattern
A rise returns the module to its first active pattern and its first step

outputs.text: A 10V trigger on each step that fires, of the length set on the menu
The velocity of the last step that fired, 0-10V, held until the next one fires
A 10V trigger on each firing step that is marked accented, of the length set on the menu

notes: the module has no knobs: patterns, step velocities, accents, probabilities, pattern length and repeat count are all edited on the display, which no click can reach for help
nothing plays until a clock is patched; the module has no tempo of its own and is meant to be driven from a Meter or any other clock
a bar pulse and a clock pulse arriving together count as one event: the clock is suppressed while the bar pulse is high, so a bar boundary does not fire two steps back to back
menu: Advance only on bar trigger — moves to the next pattern only on a real bar pulse, so with nothing patched at BAR the current pattern repeats for ever
Gate/trigger width — sets how long the gate and accent pulses last: a fixed 1, 2, 5 or 10ms
Copy current pattern — takes a copy of the pattern being edited
Copy all patterns — takes a copy of all eight patterns at once
Paste to current pattern — writes the copied pattern over the one being edited, leaving its active flag alone
Paste all patterns — writes the copied set over all eight patterns
Randomize current pattern steps — switches each of the sixteen steps on or off at even odds, leaving velocity, accent and probability alone
Clear current pattern — switches off every step of the pattern being edited and returns its velocities, accents and probabilities to their defaults
Clear all patterns — returns all eight patterns to empty and marks them all active
